title: Marcos: 29M coconut trees out of 100M target planted so far
summary: President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. said Thursday that the administration has so far planted 29 million coconut trees out of its 100 million goal by the end of his term.

blocks.text: President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. said Thursday that the administration has so far planted 29 million coconut trees out of its 100 million goal by the end of his term.
Marcos witnessed the signing of a memorandum of understanding (MOU) for a 10-million coconut tree partnership with private-sector partners.
This is to help replace aging coconut trees by providing 10 million quality seeds to 100,000 smallholder farms in Mindanao.

“As of October this year, we have planted nearly 29 million coconut palms. Reaching our goal of 100 million is not going to be an easy task, but it is worth the effort. And an effort of this scale calls for the participation of everyone, of course, including the private sector,” Marcos said in his speech in Malacañang Palace.
The President said that a large number of the country’s coconut trees were aging, with many of them planted by previous generations.

“Many of our farmers still harvest from palms that their parents and grandparents once tended. Many coconut palms in the country have already reached an age that its productivity has begun to decline,” Marcos said.
Following the President’s speech, Marcos and Agriculture Secretary Francisco "Kiko" P. Tiu Laurel Jr. presented symbolic coconut palms to two indigenous farmer beneficiaries.

Among the signatories were Philippine Coconut Authority (PCA), Metro Pacific Agro Ventures, Inc., Vita Coco Community Foundation, Century Pacific Food, Inc. (CPFI) and HOPE. The President thanked the groups for focusing on Mindanao, which accounted for more than 60% of the country’s coconut production.
Marcos said that every coconut palm that will be planted is accounted for and will be reported on HOPE’s website.
The 100 million coconut tree target has been a longtime goal for Marcos. He reiterated this goal in his 2026 State of the Nation Address. —AOL, GMA News
